title: Cluster Guardian: health-orbit canvas & burst orchestration for dedicated fleets
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design a consolidated 'Cluster Guardian' canvas for Dedicated capacity that surfaces real-time health signals, predictive stress windows, and an orchestration panel for temporary burst allocations. The goal is to give SREs and platform engineers a single surface to assess fleet resiliency, tune autoscaling policies, and authorize short-lived burst budgets with clear cost and latency trade-offs. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma prototype, interaction spec for rollouts & fallback, a small component library (status orb, ledger rows, resilience lanes), and a handoff checklist for engineering and product. Focus areas: (1) health-orbit visualization summarizing per-pool KPIs without overwhelming rows of metrics, (2) an autoscaling policy composer that previews expected throughput/latency under selected rules, (3) a burst orchestration flow including request, approve, and rollback with cost impact preview, (4) mobile/compact variants for on-call quick triage.
comments: 2025-03-12 Ava Chen: Kickoff — scoped canvas to three primary lanes: health summary, policy composer, burst ledger. Included acceptance criteria and success metrics. Linked initial PRD and asked Eng to confirm available telemetry fields.

2025-03-14 Marcus Patel (eng): Telemetry OK — can provide 90/95/99 latency, load, queue depth, and pod-level eviction rates. Suggested adding a synthetic 'stress forecast' signal from autoscaler logs.

2025-03-15 Design critique (team): Remove dense tables — replaced with 'resilience lanes' and horizontal sparkline stacks to improve scanability. Need accessible color tokens for severity levels (low/medium/high/critical).
2025-03-16 PM review (Liam O'Connor): Approved scope but requested clearer CTA for 'Request burst' to include owner and duration. Flagged cost visibility as required before approval flow.

2025-03-17 Usability testing (3 SREs): Users liked the orbit summary but wanted one-click drilldown to recent incidents. Added micro-interaction: orbit click opens incident timeline filtered to that pool.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Console displays per-pool health-orbit with latency, load, and eviction severity; 2) Autoscaling composer can simulate rule changes and show expected throughput/latency; 3) Burst request flow prompts for owner/duration and shows cost delta before submit; 4) Interaction spec delivered and engineering sign-off obtained; 5) Accessibility contrast and keyboard flows validated.
next_steps: Finalize high-fidelity screens and handoff tokens by 2025-03-19; schedule implementation sync with ENG on 2025-03-20; set up feature flag gating and Canary rollout plan with PM.
design_notes: Avoid red/green only indicators; use combined icon + color + text severity. 'Orbit' should be semantic: inner ring = immediate criticality, outer rings = trend windows (1h, 24h). Burst ledger modeled after financial ledger rows with editable approvals. Provide granular presets for common burst scenarios (short spike, scheduled batch, maintenance drain).
review_feedback: Marcus Patel: Good overall. Engineering ask: make orbit payload minimal — 12 fields max. Liam O'Connor: Add audit trail entry for each burst approval (user, time, duration, cost). Accessibility review: ensure orbit SVG aria-labels and focusable sectors.
risks: Telemetry gaps for older pools may show 'unknown' state; fallback UI must surface missing data gracefully. Burst approvals can be abused — product to design rate limits and RBAC scoping. Autoscaler simulation is approximate; must include 'confidence' band in UI.
outcomes: Expected outcomes are faster incident triage (reduce on-call resolution time by ~20%), clearer cost-preview for bursts, and fewer emergency scale-ups without documented approvals.
notes_for_engineering: Deliver three API endpoints: /health-orbit (summary), /autoscale-simulate (policy preview), /burst-request (create/approve/rollback). Provide example payloads in the Handoff doc in Figma file. Engineering to own final performance budget for orbit refresh rate (target: 5s for active pools).
